The exact midpoint 0.025 tells HALF_UP (0.03) apart from HALF_EVEN (0.02).
Calls the method on Cart() with no items and expects ValueError. ZeroDivisionError is not a ValueError subclass, so an unguarded division would fail the test.

findings.title: No scenario covers the average when a discount code is applied
findings.detail: The requirement text says to use the subtotal, and the implementation does: it calls self.subtotal(), not total(). No scenario checks a cart with a code applied, so an implementation that used the discounted total would pass every test. The current code follows the requirement text.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scenario stating that applied discounts do not affect the average unit price.

findings.title: Tests do not check the scale or type of the result
findings.detail: Decimal("2.5") == Decimal("2.50") is true, and so are equality comparisons between float and Decimal values that are exactly equal. The tests therefore do not show that the result is a Decimal quantized to two places; the evidence for that is the quantize call and the return annotation. Q-001 settled the return type (Decimal), but no scenario requires it.
findings.suggested_fix: Also assert isinstance(result, Decimal) and result.as_tuple().exponent == -2.
